# Reference scaling suites: Pythia and Cerebras-GPT

These are designed scaling suites, not labs with an experiments-vs-final split. They give clean
reference curves on a public dataset (the Pile) against which the lab chapters can be read.

```{python}
#| echo: false
from src.chapter import *  # noqa
```

## Pythia (EleutherAI)

70M to 12B, same 300B tokens in the same order, 154 checkpoints per model.

```{python}
df_p = load.runs("eleutherai", "pythia")
fit_p = fits.fit_power_law(df_p["flops"], df_p["loss"], irreducible=True) if len(df_p.dropna(subset=["flops","loss"])) >= 3 else None
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5)); plots.scaling_curve(df_p, fit=fit_p, ax=ax, title="Pythia: loss vs compute"); plt.show()
if fit_p: display(Markdown(f"Fitted: `{fit_p.label()}`. Elasticity at the 12B run: {fit_p.elasticity(df_p['flops'].max()):.3f}"))
```

## Cerebras-GPT

Seven sizes, 111M to 13B, trained compute-optimally; the lab publishes its own fitted law.

```{python}
df_c = load.runs("cerebras", "cerebras-gpt")
fit_c = fits.fit_power_law(df_c["flops"], df_c["loss"], irreducible=True) if len(df_c.dropna(subset=["flops","loss"])) >= 3 else None
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5)); plots.scaling_curve(df_c, fit=fit_c, ax=ax, title="Cerebras-GPT: loss vs compute"); plt.show()
if fit_c: display(Markdown(f"Fitted: `{fit_c.label()}`."))
```

## Both suites on one axis

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
plots.overlay_projects({"Pythia": df_p, "Cerebras-GPT": df_c}, {"Pythia": fit_p, "Cerebras-GPT": fit_c}, ax=ax, title="Reference suites (Pile loss)")
plt.show()
```

## Published fits and key numbers

```{python}
experiments_table("eleutherai"); experiments_table("cerebras");
```
